en.name: NearServe
en.short_description: Find local plumbers, electricians, tutors and more from OpenStreetMap
en.subtitle: Local services directory
en.description:
NearServe finds local service providers near a town or postcode you choose: plumbers, electricians, cleaners, hairdressers, mechanics, doctors and dentists, tutors, vets, lawyers, caterers, movers and gyms. Listings are real businesses from OpenStreetMap, the community-built map. Nothing is invented: anything OpenStreetMap does not publish is shown as not published.

FIND
Pick a category or search for a trade. Each listing shows what OpenStreetMap contributors have published: address, phone number, website, opening hours and distance from your area. Tap to call or to open the website. OpenStreetMap carries no prices or ratings, so NearServe shows none: no price, no cost estimate and no star rating appears for these listings.

PLAN
For a business that publishes regular opening hours, pick a time inside those hours and keep it in your Bookings. NearServe does not contact the business or make a reservation for you. Call them to arrange it.

AFTER
Your planned appointments live in one place. Once an appointment time has passed you can write a review of it; reviews are stored on your device only.

SAVED
Keep the providers you would use again. Everything you save stays on your device, and NearServe has no account.

Listing data © OpenStreetMap contributors.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
NearServe finds local service providers near a town or postcode the user chooses. Listings are real businesses from OpenStreetMap; the app contains no invented listings, prices or ratings. Appointments the user plans are kept on the device only and are not sent to the business.

Intended audience:
People looking for a local tradesperson or service near them.

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
No account and no login are required.
1. On first launch, tap 'Choose your area', type a town or postcode (for example 'Austin, TX') and tap the match.
2. Browse shows 12 categories. Tap one (for example Plumbing) to load real businesses within 10 miles from OpenStreetMap. The Search tab also finds them by trade, e.g. 'dentist'.
3. Open a listing to call the business, open its website, or save it. When the business publishes regular opening hours, 'Book a slot' keeps a planned appointment in the Bookings tab; the business is not contacted.
4. Settings shows the chosen area and lets the user change it. 'Delete my data on this device' removes the bookings, reviews, saved providers and chosen area stored on the device; the theme and language settings are kept.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
OpenStreetMap public services, with no key and no account:
- Nominatim (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) turns the town or postcode the user types into coordinates.
- The Overpass API (overpass-api.de, with overpass.private.coffee as a fallback) returns businesses near those coordinates.
Only the typed place name and its coordinates are sent. The app does not read the device location. Listing data © OpenStreetMap contributors, credited in the app.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
Features are identical in every region; listings depend on what OpenStreetMap has mapped in the chosen area. The language picker offers 12 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish). The tab bar and shared labels are translated; most other screen text is currently English.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry and carries no licensed third-party material. All content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app creates no account, so there is nothing to delete.

Yes, infrastructure only: agl_i18n (shared translations); agl_observability (crash reporting). It has no sign-in and uses no backend of ours; listings come from the public OpenStreetMap services. No screens, features or content are shared; the similarity figure in 5 measures exactly that.
